implementation: Default-off SRPT prefill order with a bypass cap and one-slice contention
modifications: Reimplemented as a host-only Python policy (PrefillOrder) beside DecodeTimeFairness; no Splash code was copied.

Splash packs several shortest prompts into one command; mlx2 keeps its admission shapes: the ordinary path moves SRPT picks to the queue head before the state-budget check, and the self-MTP path picks one lane per round.
Splash's overtake bound is a fixed batch width minus one; mlx2 makes it a server-owned max_bypass (default 3) and serves the oldest overdue request first.

Splash's contended 500 ms slice bound reuses DecodeTimeFairness.stall_bound (same measured-throughput grid formula) so one-slice contention and decode fairness share one measurement; decode debt is still accrued and repaid only for decode contention.
A candidate fits one slice only after mlx2 APC interior-checkpoint boundaries clamp its chunk; declared batch cohorts keep main's atomic path and never take the SRPT short-promotion branch.
Disabled, PrefillOrder.select reproduces main's self-MTP shortest-residual key exactly; the ordinary path stays FIFO.
validation: CPU tests in tests/test_srpt_prefill.py cover parsing, the disabled key's equivalence to main, the bypass cap on both the policy and the real self-MTP and ordinary schedulers (both fail with the cap lifted), short-request TTFT behind a 64k-token prefill, one-slice clamping with and without the rule and with an interior-checkpoint boundary, cohort atomicity, route rejection and the qualification feature.
